This is why Rambam's wording, and the corrected wording of the Shulchan Aruch according to Sema, does not make release from the ban depend upon whether the injured party personally accepts the payment. If strict Torah law required the full amount, his willingness to be appeased would not control it. The Tur and Rosh indicate that Rav Sherira Gaon's rule is only a Geonic enactment and not the law of the Gemara itself. Therefore, if the tortfeasor dies, his son should not be placed under a ban. The enactment was made to restrain violent offenders and prevent damage in the world. It is enough to penalize the wrongdoer himself; the son who did nothing should not be added to the enactment.
And likewise if he seized, etc. He may seize even an object other than the thing that caused the injury. However, with a tam ox, whose liability is paid from the body of the animal itself, Mordechai cites Ri Baal HaTosafos as inclined to Rabbeinu Tam's view that only the damaging animal itself is subject to seizure. See Tumim. Seizure can also secure double payment and fourfold or fivefold payment. If he did not seize, however, the offender is placed under a ban. Once he pays an amount close to the principal loss, the ban is lifted. Sema, against Ir Shushan. If the offender admitted liability, seizure is not automatically defeated merely because the admission was not before an ordained beit din. Sema and Shach write that nowadays every admission is effectively outside beit din because we lack ordained judges. But in Yoreh Deah, siman 267, Shach himself challenges this and agrees with Beit Yosef that an admission defeats collection of a fine only where witnesses later arrive. If no witnesses later arrive, one of two things is true: either the admission has no judicial force and the claimant has no basis for seizure, or it is a valid admission and then he has admitted a fine. Nimukei Yosef in Perek Merubah says this explicitly, and this is the correct view. Shach cites Ramban in Milchamot that if a depositary falsely claims theft and is himself the thief, thereby becoming liable for double payment, seizure by the owner does not help, because liability for the double payment arises only after an oath before beit din. In this respect we have no competent beit din nowadays. Maharshal writes that one should not seize through a non Jewish authority. He does not clarify whether, after the fact, such seizure is effective. I will discuss that elsewhere.
We do not listen to him. Maharshal distinguishes between a true fine, which we do not adjudicate, and an ordinary monetary claim that we cannot adjudicate merely because it is uncommon. For a fine, we do not make an appraisal before seizure, following the Rosh. For an ordinary monetary claim that is simply outside our current jurisdiction because it is uncommon, we appraise immediately so the claimant knows how much he may seize. Shach.
Return such and such. Darchei Moshe and Sema reject Mahari Weil's ruling that because we are not expert in valuation, the claimant may retain everything seized. The Rosh's procedure is to appraise and require return of the excess. Mahari Weil's language would imply that when beit din cannot make a reliable valuation, the claimant may retain property because of the doubt. In my opinion, anything beyond the amount of damage clearly established cannot be retained. See Tumim. Sema writes that if the seizure occurred before witnesses, the claimant must prove the amount of damage. If the seizure occurred without witnesses, so that he has a migo of complete denial or return, he is believed regarding the amount owed him because of the damage, whether principal or fine, through that migo. Even concerning a fine, a valid migo can establish his claim, as explained below in siman 359.
With fines written in the Torah, etc. Although Torah fines are not collected nowadays, local communal authorities may adjudicate them through the seven good men of the city. Sema in the name of Mordechai. It appears that this requires the agreement of the communal Torah scholar as well.
But fines instituted by the Sages. See Tumim, where I distinguished between common and uncommon matters. An uncommon matter is not collected outside Eretz Yisrael even in such circumstances. A judge may, however, impose a penalty payable to the government upon one who refuses to obey Torah law. Sema in the name of Terumat HaDeshen. This point requires careful qualification.

mechaber.he: המבייש בדברים מנדין אותו עד שיפייסנו כראוי לפי כבודו: הגה וע' לקמן סי' ת"כ סעיף ל"ח וע' לקמן סי' ב' אם נתחייב לו מלקות אם יכול לפדות עצמו בממון:
mechaber.en: He is ashamed of the things that he is treated until he is properly identified by his honor: G-d and Lman C. A. C. C. B. If he commits to him if he can burn himself in a crowd:

baer_hetev.he:
בדברים. זהו מתקנת הגאונים אבל מדינא פטור בבושת דברים ואפי' דיינים סמוכים אין גובין אותו. סמ"ע:
כבודו. בירושלמי הביאו הטור דמבייש את הזקן נותן ליטרא דדהבא וי"מ שהוא ל"ו זהובים עכ"ל סמ"ע וכ' הש"ך דבי"ד סי' רמ"ג ס"ב פסק הרמ"א שאין לנו בזה"ז דין ת"ח לענין ליטרא דדהבא אבל בתשובת ר"י מטראני החדשים ס"ס מ"ז חולק ע"ז ע"ש:
baer_hetev.en:
In things. This is the gestation of the geniuses, but a fraud is exempted by shame of things, and a neighboring Khamenei does not understand it. A:
His honor. The Yerushalmi, cited by the Tur, states that one who humiliates an elder must pay a litra of gold; some explain this as 36 gold coins. Thus concludes the Sema. The Shach writes that in Yoreh Deah, siman 243, seif 2, the Rama rules that nowadays a Torah scholar does not have the status of a talmid chacham for purposes of the litra of gold. Responsa Maharit HaChadashot, end of siman 47, disagrees. See there.

beer_hagolah.he: ר) טור בשם רב שרירא גאון

beur_hagra.he: המבייש. רא"ש פ' החובל מגמ' ערכין ט"ו א':
beur_hagra.en: One who humiliates. This is from the Rosh in HaChovel, based on the Gemara in Arakhin 15a.

chelkat_mechokek.he: והוא שלא יהיה הבן סריס וכו'. נראה דאם הבן נשא איילונית או הבת נשאת לסריס או שלא נשאו כלל קיים האב פ"ו דאל"כ ליתני רבותא:
chelkat_mechokek.en: He will not be the son of Sris and so on. It seems that if the son was carrying an ailton or the daughter was carrying to Saras or not carrying any of the father P. and D.D. for me:

meirat_einayim.he:
המבייש בדברים גם זה כתב הטור בשם רב שרירא והרא"ש והוא מתקנת הגאונים אבל מדינא פטור בבושת דברים ואפי' בדיינים סמוכים אין גובין ממנו בושת מן הדין כדאיתא בפ' החובל (בבא קמא דף צ"א ע"א) ולא כמ"ש בע"ש ע"ש:
לפי כבודו בירושלמי (הביאו הטור) דמבייש את הזקן נותן לו ליטרא דדהבא עכ"ל והוא משקל ל"ה דינרי זהב כמ"ש הרמב"ם הביאו הטור לקמן בסי' ת"ך סעיף ל' שכתב וגובין ממנו ל"ה דינרי זהובים ומוכח ממאי דמסיק שם אחר זה דהוא ליטרא זהב ע"ש וי"מ שהוא ל"ו זהובים כמ"ש בי"ד סימן של"ד בשם מהר"ם מ"ץ:
meirat_einayim.en:
One who humiliates another verbally. The Tur cites this in the name of Rav Sherira and the Rosh. It is an enactment of the Geonim. By strict law, verbal humiliation carries no monetary payment, and even ordained judges would not collect damages for words alone, as stated in chapter HaChovel, Bava Kamma 91a. This is unlike Ir Shushan.
According to his honor. The Yerushalmi, cited by the Tur, states that one who humiliates an elder pays a litra of gold. A litra is the weight of thirty-five gold dinars, as Rambam explains and the Tur cites below in siman 420, seif 30. Some explain it as thirty-six gold coins, as cited in Yoreh Deah siman 334 in the name of Maharam of Rothenburg.

netivot_hamishpat_beurim.he: אבל קנסות שבאים חכמים לקנוס וכו' בתומים הקשה דבי"ד סי' רס"ז פסק גבי המוכר עבדו דאין קונסין אותו ונראה דהרמ"א הכריע דאותן השנויים במשנה וברייתא י"ל דבעי' דוקא סמוכין אבל בהקנסות שכ' המרדכי פרק השולח מהא דהגוזל קמא דאמר ר"ג גזלנא עתיקא הוא ובעינא למיקנסיה. ורש"י פי' בכתובות דף מ"ג דכ"מ שנקרא רב לא היה מוסמך דנין אותו ככ"מ ומזה נלמוד ג"כ במה שרוצין החכמים לקנוס על תקנתם בזה"ז כדמייתי התם המרדכי ראיה מהא דמכין ועונשין שלא מן הדין ע"ש:
netivot_hamishpat_beurim.en:
But fines that come to Kanus and so on in the harsh records of D.C., the sellers have worked on, and it seems to be called Dr. D.C., and it seems that the D.C. has made it clear, but in the same fines as the rebel section of the sender from the Dagosel Kama, an ancient gas and anail. And according to the scriptures of a page called Rabbi Danin, he was not authorized as negotiations, and he was measured in what the Sages had arranged for the Consummation
Hashem's mercy and mercy that is not Hashem's judgment

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: לפי כבודו. כ' בי"ד דהמבייש ת"ח קונסין אותו ליטרא דדהבא והרמ"א כ' דאין לת"ח שבזמנינו דין זה. וכבר פיקפק ע"ז בתשו' מוהרי"ט אבל מ"מ ראוי לדיין להתאמץ מאוד בזה להעניש בעונש עצום להמבייש ת"ח ואדרבה אשר בעו"ה בלא"ה נדלדל חכמת התורה אם לא יכניסו הב"ד עצמם לקנוס למבייש ת"ח יהיה ח"ו תורה נבזה למאד ויקוצו הלומדים להגות בה ח"ו. או"ת:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: According to his honor. Yoreh Deah states that one who humiliates a Torah scholar is fined a litra of gold. Rama writes that Torah scholars of our time do not have this law. Maharit already questioned that ruling. Nevertheless, a judge should exert himself greatly in this matter and impose a very severe punishment upon one who humiliates a Torah scholar. On the contrary, especially because, due to our sins, Torah wisdom has already declined, if beit din does not involve itself in penalizing those who disgrace Torah scholars, Torah will become greatly despised and students will become disgusted with studying it, Heaven forbid. Urim VeTumim.

pitchei_teshuva.he: אין מוציאין מידו. בגליון ש"ע דהגר"ע זצ"ל נ"ב ונעשה ממונו ממש ואפי' חזר המזיק ותפס הימנו לא מהני. וש"ש פ"ק דב"ק סי' מ"ג עכ"ל וע' בנה"מ מזה:
pitchei_teshuva.en: We do not remove it from his possession. Rabbi Akiva Eiger notes in his glosses to Shulchan Aruch that it becomes fully his property, and even if the damager subsequently seizes it back from him, the seizure is ineffective. See Shitah Mekubetzet to the first chapter of Bava Kamma, siman 43. See also Netivot HaMishpat on this matter.

siftei_kohen.he:
[" לפי כבודו (הג\"ה בירושלמי הביאו הטור דהמבייש הזקן נותן לו ליטרא דדהבא עכ\"ל ומביאו בסמ\"ע ופסק מור\"ם בי\"ד בסי' רמ\"ג ס\"ב בהג\"ה שאין לת\"ח בזמן הזה דין ת\"ח לענין ליטרא דדהבא והוא מת\"ה וכ\"כ מהרי\"ק שורש קס\"ג ובתשו' ר\"י מטראני החדשים ס\"ס מ\"ז חולק ע\"ז ודחה בשתי ידים וס\"ל שיש לו דין ת\"ח לענין ליטרא דדהבא ועיין עוד שם):"]
[" וע\"ל סי' ת\"ך כו' וסימן כ\"ז ס\"ב:"]
siftei_kohen.en:
According to his honor. Gloss: The Yerushalmi, cited by the Tur, states that one who humiliates an elder pays him a litra of gold. The Sema cites this. Rama rules in Yoreh Deah, siman 243, seif 2, that a Torah scholar nowadays does not have the status of a Torah scholar regarding a litra of gold. This is based on Terumat HaDeshen, and Maharik, shoresh 163, writes similarly. Responsa Maharit, new responsa, end of siman 47, strongly disagrees and holds that he does have the status of a Torah scholar regarding a litra of gold. See further there.
See below, siman 420, etc. And siman 27, seif 2.

turei_zahav.he: (תו איתא שם). אבל ריפוי ושבת דכין משמע דפגם אין דנין דפגם היינו נזק וקשה דבפ' החובל דף פ"ד פריך פגם ובשת דשכיח כעביד שליחותייהו דשכיח הוא ומשני אין ה"נ דהא רב פפא אגבי בשת ופריך והא ליתא לדרב פפא מדרב חסדא כו' ומסקינן לא עבדינן שליחותייהו רק בשכיח ויש בו ח"כ הלכך בשת דאין ח"כ לא עברינן שליחותייהו משמע דבפגם קיימא סברת המקשן דשכיח הוא ועבדינן שליחותייהו. ונראה דהאי פגם הוא טעות בגמ' אלא מבשת לחוד פריך אבל פגם ודאי לא שכיח ותדע דאי פריך מפגם קשה מי הגיד לו באמת שאין דנין אותו כיון דשכיח הוא בשלמא בבושת סמך המקשן על מה שהקשה אח"כ מדרב חסדא משא"כ בפגם אלא ודאי ט"ס הוא כן נ"ל ברור:
turei_zahav.en: It is further stated there. The wording “but medical expenses and loss of work are adjudicated” implies that depreciation is not adjudicated, and depreciation means bodily damage. This is difficult, because in the chapter HaChovel, Bava Kamma 84b, the Gemara asks that depreciation and humiliation are common, and therefore the judges of Babylonia should act as the agents of the ordained judges. It answers that this is indeed so, for Rav Pappa collected humiliation damages. The Gemara then challenges Rav Pappa's ruling from Rav Chisda and concludes that the judges of Babylonia act as agents only in a common matter that also entails a monetary loss. Humiliation, which does not entail a monetary loss, is therefore not adjudicated. This implies that regarding depreciation the questioner's assumption remains, namely, that it is common and is adjudicated. It appears that the word “depreciation” in the Gemara is a scribal error, and that the question was asked only from humiliation. Depreciation is certainly uncommon. This is also evident, for if the question included depreciation, how did the questioner know that it was not adjudicated, seeing that he himself considered it common? Regarding humiliation, however, the questioner relied upon the challenge subsequently brought from Rav Chisda. No such source exists regarding depreciation. It is therefore certainly a textual error, and this appears clear to me.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: לפ"כ. כבר כתב המחבר בי"ד דמבייש ת"ח קונסין אותו ליטרא דדהב' והרמ"א כ' דאין לת"ח בזמנינו דין זה וכבר פקפק ע"ז בתשובת מהרי"ט ומ"מ נראה דאף דאין לקנוס ליטרא דדהב' אבל מ"מ ראוי לדיין להתאמץ מאוד בזה להעניש בעונש עצום להמבייש ת"ח ואדרבה אשר בעו"ה בלא"ה נדלדל חכמת התורה אם לא יכניסו הב"ד עצמן לקנוס למבייש לת"ח יהיה ח"ו תורה נבזה למאוד ויקוצו הלומדי' להגות בו ח"ו:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: Accordingly. Mechaber writes in Yoreh Deah that one who humiliates a Torah scholar can be fined a litra of gold. Rama says that scholars today do not have this status. Maharit questions that limitation. Even if we do not impose the historic fixed fine of a litra of gold, a judge should nevertheless exert himself greatly to punish one who humiliates a Torah scholar. In our sins, Torah scholarship has already been diminished. If beit din fails to punish contempt for scholars, Torah itself will become despised and students will lose the desire to devote themselves to it.
